Team — forwarding Kirti's ask. Summary and proposed approach below. I need approvals from Ben (credits / customer terms) and Laura (contract/legal) by EOD PT so we can confirm to Cerulean.

Problem: APAC maintenance 00:00–06:00 SGT on 2026-07-18 overlaps Cerulean's higher-than-normal traffic period. There is a potential shortfall in our regular APAC primary on-call headcount for that window.

Proposed temporary bridging plan (operational):
- Shifted standby: shadow on-call rotation for 00:00–04:00 SGT will be covered by EU primary (Grace) and US late-shift volunteers for 04:00–06:00 SGT.
- Hot-seat escalation: designate a P1 hot-seat (single engineer) per 2-hour block; hot-seat owner will be reachable by phone and must acknowledge within 15 minutes.
- Routing fallback: auto-fallback to a warm standby model variant in another region in case of capacity degradations (no data-copy; config controlled routing).
- Runbook: attach APAC-maintenance-rotational-plan.pdf with explicit contact tree, Slack bridge channel (#ops-cerulean-apac), and escalation ladder.

SLA / commercial mitigations (Ben):
- Recommend offering a partial SLO credit for the maintenance window if Cerulean experiences a verified P1 response delay beyond our SLOs. Proposed credit: pro-rated service credit equivalent to 4 hours of token usage capped at $X (will confirm exact calculation).
- Flagging: we should avoid changing core contractual SLAs; this is an exception with documented acceptance by customer.

Contract/legal (Laura):
- We need a one-off SLO exception addendum signed or written acceptance (email suffices) before maintenance. Can you confirm minimal wording we need and whether we require an internal legal sign-off?

Questions for the group:
1) Ben — confirm willingness to commit to the proposed credit cap and approve push to customer.
2) Laura — do we require an addendum doc or is email acceptance acceptable for this scale?
3) Grace — can you confirm EU team coverage for the first half of the maintenance window and provide a named primary?
